name: false-decision-trap

items.title: Dashboard performance approach
items.summary: Decide whether the dashboard performance problem needs a rewrite or a targeted rendering fix; there is no consensus yet.
items.tradeoff: Targeted performance fix even over a full framework rewrite until evidence shows the framework is the bottleneck.
items.why: The decision question appears only after the group reframes the strong preference into a real tradeoff, and the transcript explicitly says approval is not being requested today.

items.summary: Ask what evidence shows the framework is the bottleneck rather than data loading or chart rendering.
items.useful_friction: Prevents a strong preference from becoming a rewrite decision before evidence is collected.
items.human_judgment_role: Helps the team ask for disconfirming evidence without letting the agent decide the technical path.
items.why: The cue names the central assumption that would determine whether rewrite is justified.

should_not_emit: Do not emit an accepted decision to rewrite the dashboard.
If a forming decision is captured, it must indicate there is no consensus yet.
Do not capture Alex's dislike of component patterns as a decision or risk.
Do not emit an action for collecting measurements because no owner or timing is assigned.
